summary.headline: Manorama Q1 FY27 revenue rose 39.5% YoY to INR 404 crore and PAT rose 67.6% to INR 79 crore, with PAT margin at 19.5%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 39.5% YoY to INR 404 crore, crossing INR 400 crore for the first time, with management attributing growth mainly to volume (about 85% YoY per management). EBITDA rose 42.2% to INR 106 crore at a 26.3% margin, and PAT rose 67.6% to INR 79 crore. Management said the QIP of about INR 500 crore has closed and it has lined up a ~INR 460 crore capex plan spanning India and Burkina Faso, with commissioning targeted around Q3 FY28. Several answers were qualitative or deferred, notably on guidance, Brazil revenue, and subsidiary losses.

segments.name: Value-added specialty fats (CBE and stearin)
segments.commentary: Management said CBE is about 30% and stearin about 70% of the contribution from these products; per-ton realisations were not shared, but pricing was described as largely stable.

segments.name: Subsidiaries (consolidated vs standalone)
segments.commentary: Consolidated PAT loss narrowed to about INR 3 crore from about INR 8 crore in Q4 FY26, with negligible subsidiary revenue; West African entities are sourcing vehicles and Brazil is in build-out.

guidance_outlook: FY27 utilisation guidance is about 80% (management internal target 80-85%) on expanded capacity of about 52,000 tonnes per annum after 4,500 t debottlenecking; the company declined to restate the INR 1,600-1,800 crore revenue guidance from November, pointing to utilisation metrics instead.
FY27 capex guidance of about INR 225-250 crore; about INR 70 crore spent to date and about INR 220 crore more planned in FY27.

Gross margin expected in a 45-50% range, with EBITDA margin the preferred tracking metric; management said margins should hold broadly stable at current range, with quarter-to-quarter movement possible.

Burkina Faso facility (about INR 120-130 crore) has an estimated payback of about 3 years once operational; the remainder of the ~INR 460 crore plan is for India (solvent fractionation 3 and refinery).
Solvent fractionation 3 and refinery targeted for commissioning around Q3 FY28; full impact expected in FY29 as plants ramp up.
Balance sheet: no further equity dilution planned; working capital to be funded via existing banker lines led by SBI, plus ~INR 150 crore FDR outside the QIP proceeds.
capex_capacity: Current fractionation capacity 47,500 t per annum; additional 7,500 t already operational, with a further 4,500 t debottlenecking targeted around Q3 FY27, taking capacity to about 52,000 t.
Debottlenecking cost estimated at INR 5-6 crore.

Burkina Faso: about 10 hectares (24 acres) land acquired for shea nut and mango nut processing with regulatory approvals pending; facility covers extraction and expelling, solvent fractionation and related capacity, about INR 120-130 crore.
Overall proposed capex plan about INR 460 crore; about INR 70 crore spent to date; Q1 spend about INR 20 crore across Manorama and subsidiaries.
Brazil (LatAm) partner: trial production started in the last quarter; ramp-up expected gradually over the next 2-4 quarters, with production sourced from the Indian plant.
Asset turn currently about 7x; management would not guide to 7x-9x going forward.
demand_pricing: Demand described as volume-led; management attributed about 85% YoY growth to volume.
Pricing described as largely stable for value-added products, in line with the costing model that passes through raw material inflation.
Raw material mix: about 50-60% imported seeds and butters, the rest domestic seeds (sal, mango) and butters.
Contracts are 9-12 months and renew on a rolling basis; no renewal percentage was disclosed.
Nigeria's temporary shea nut export ban was called non-material given sourcing across about 10 African subsidiaries.
Exports to more than 30 countries; export share about 55-60% in Q1 FY25 and 60% in Q1 FY27 per management.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of the 4,500 t debottlenecking and greenfield capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Debottlenecking is due around Q3 FY27; solvent fractionation 3 and refinery are targeted around Q3 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Brazil ramp-up and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production started; gradual quarter-on-quarter ramp expected over 2-4 quarters; no revenue guidance given yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall about 20% QoQ, and is it the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Prior quarter included a performance incentive provision; run-rate guided at INR 14-15 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin decline and raw material cost ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin expected at 45-50%; management disputed the 75-80% H1 raw material ratio, saying it has been about 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated subsidiary losses and whether they will narrow?
qa_highlights.answer: Losses reflect operating costs of sourcing vehicles and Brazil build-out; drag expected to reduce as entities scale, with no timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Utilisation guidance versus the 85-90% cited in the presentation?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal target 80-85%; 80% advised for stakeholders, with upside to be communicated if achieved.

qa_highlights.question: Funding of working capital for the new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Funded by existing bank lines (SBI lead), the QIP of about INR 500 crore and FDR of about INR 150 crore; no further equity dilution planned.

risks_watch: Supplier dispute: a debit note has been raised for the full claim amount against a foreign manufacturer/supplier, with no recovery timeline or confirmation of liability given.
Geopolitical and freight disruption; management said freight and container costs drove the 16% jump in other expenses.
Utilisation target ambiguity (80% vs 85-90%) and withdrawal of the INR 1,600-1,800 crore revenue guidance.
Subsidiary and Brazil losses weigh on consolidated margins; timing of breakeven undisclosed.
Working capital needs for new capacity (analyst estimate INR 900-1,000 crore) and reliance on bank lines.
Hedging policy of 50-60% of net exposure; forex gains formed about INR 13 crore of the INR 16 crore other income, so the earnings quality of other income is a watch item.
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline growth and capacity build-out, but evasive on forward numbers: management repeatedly declined to quantify margins, revenue guidance, Brazil contribution, subsidiary breakeven, and per-ton realisations, redirecting to utilisation and "business has risk" framing.
